newsitem.title: BURMA: Burmese students demonstrate against authorities.
newsitem.headline: Burmese students demonstrate against authorities.

text.p: About 500 Burmese university students demonstrated early on Wednesday against the military government's handling of a scuffle on Sunday between students and staff of a food shop, witnesses said.

The demonstration, the first major protest by students in several years, was against the detention of three students and the way they were treated by police, they told Reuters. The three-hour demonstration ended peacefully.

The demonstrating students had said that government broadcasts on Tuesday night of the arrests of the three students were inaccurate and that police had manhandled those detained. They demanded an apology from the police within 48 hours.

The students were persuaded to disperse by teachers and education ministry officials. They also wanted the government to broadcast a chronology of the events leading to the detention and the release of students who were held, witnesses said.

The ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC), issued a statement accusing the students of having met with officials of democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy (NLD) party before holding the protest.
Witnesses said the SLORC again blocked access to Suu Kyi's University Avenue home by closing off roads leading to it on Tuesday night, a day after it had been reopened following 10 days of closure.
